scenes.title: St Andrews fMRI Control Suite: Triggering Artificial Déjà Vu in 16 of 21 Scanned Adults as Frontal Fact-Checkers Ignite
scenes.era: 2018–2021, School of Psychology and Neuroscience fMRI Suite, University of St Andrews, Scotland

layout.description: Crisp sunlit-glass fMRI control room overlooking a white cylindrical 3T MRI scanner bore: inside the bore a volunteer grips a fiber-optic two-button response grip beneath an overhead angled mirror, while Akira O'Connor and Josephine Urquhart watch frontal cingulate-prefrontal activation light up on dual workstation monitors.

positions.who: Akira O'Connor & Josephine Urquhart (researchers in smart Scottish knitwear and lab ID lanyards)
positions.where: standing at the glass observation console pointing to the glowing frontal-cortex slice while the hippocampal slice stays dark
positions.facing: looking from the fMRI workstation through the observation glass toward the scanner bore

positions.where: lying on the cushioned MRI table looking up into the periscope mirror and pressing the right-hand 'New + Déjà Vu' button grip
positions.facing: upward toward the overhead word-projection mirror

props.name: fiber-optic MRI button-response grip and overhead mirror display
props.period_detail: non-magnetic clinical fMRI ergonomic response pad wired to control-room timing rack
props.physical_behavior: State-A thumb rests neutral on button pad while missing-theme cues finish -> State-B thumb presses decisively down on the déjà vu trigger button as frontal scan slice lights up

props.name: dual-monitor fMRI brain-slice console contrasting frontal cortex vs silent hippocampus
props.period_detail: St Andrews neuroimaging workstation beside printed word-list protocol clipboard
props.physical_behavior: State-A baseline grey brain cross-section on screen -> State-B anterior cingulate and prefrontal regions flare bright cyan while researcher taps clipboard

actions.verb_sequence: listens through padded scanner headphones -> spots the unpresented theme word in the overhead mirror and presses the déjà vu response button firmly
leans toward the workstation monitor, traces from the dark hippocampus up to the bright frontal lobe, and logs trial 16 of 21

reactions.reaction: exchange a surprised grin seeing frontal conflict-checkers—not memory storage—driving the scan
widens eyes in unmistakable recognition-without-recall wonder inside the bore

scenes.wardrobe: Modern UK university attire: charcoal merino cardigan over collared shirt; soft cotton MRI-safe scrub top on volunteer.
scenes.lighting: Clean bright clinical daylight balanced with cool sapphire monitor glow.
scenes.recognition_hook: Trigger déjà vu live inside an MRI scanner, and the memory center stays dark while your forehead's fact-checker blazes to life.

key_visual.description: a neuroimaging control room overlooking a white fMRI scanner where researchers point to bright frontal-lobe activation while a volunteer inside presses a handheld déjà vu response button

scenes.title: Outdoor Sunlit Cobblestone Travel Courtyard: Stopping Mid-Stride at a Twin Geometric Layout
scenes.era: Modern sunlit morning European/coastal stone courtyard cafe

layout.description: Open-air sunlit stone plaza with a round fountain at center, striped awning cafe tables on the left, and an arched stone passageway on the right—matching the exact 3D spacing of a forgotten hometown garden.

positions.who: 50-year-old traveler carrying a leather weekend bag and folded paper city map
positions.where: stopping dead in the middle of the sunlit stone courtyard, lowering sunglasses to scan the fountain-to-archway triangle
positions.facing: looking across the open outdoor courtyard

props.name: folded paper city map and leather weekend shoulder bag
props.period_detail: first-time visitor travel gear proving the traveler just arrived in town
props.physical_behavior: State-A traveler walks briskly unfolding crisp new city map -> State-B freezes mid-stride lowering map slowly as uncanny courtyard familiarity strikes

actions.verb_sequence: steps into the sunlit plaza unfolding a crisp map -> halts mid-step, lowers the map to waist height, and turns head left-to-right checking the fountain and cafe arch

reactions.reaction: touches temple with a fascinated smile as the frontal fact-check vetoes the false familiarity

scenes.wardrobe: Linen travel jacket over navy polo shirt and chinos.
scenes.lighting: Warm golden morning outdoor courtyard sunlight with crisp shadows.
scenes.recognition_hook: A brand-new town square shares the invisible floorplan of a forgotten place—your temporal lobe yells 'familiar!' and your forehead yells 'impossible!'

scenes.title: Fact-Checked Déjà Vu vs Unchecked False Memory: Vetoing the Illusion
scenes.era: Modern bright home living room morning coffee table

layout.description: Sunlit morning breakfast table with two ceramic coffee mugs and an open morning newspaper.

positions.where: pausing mid-pour with the coffee carafe as a dinner-table phrase triggers a 2-second déjà vu flash, then smiling and setting the carafe down calmly

props.name: glass pour-over coffee carafe and ceramic mug
props.physical_behavior: State-A hand tilts carafe to pour morning coffee -> State-B pauses two seconds mid-air during déjà vu flash, then finishes pouring smoothly and sets carafe down

actions.verb_sequence: pauses pouring coffee for two seconds as déjà vu strikes -> chuckles, finishes pouring cleanly, and sets the glass carafe onto the coaster

reactions.reaction: relaxed reassurance knowing the 2-second chill proved sharp frontal quality control

scenes.recognition_hook: That weird two-second shiver isn't your memory breaking—it's your brain refusing to buy a fake memory.
